A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Nullu and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Their corresponding content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-mitigation experiments, general-capability evaluations, ablations, and case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds an online feature-intervention example in Section 4.5 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: v3 adds a limited online inference variant that applies the learned HalluSpace projection directly to features before a hallucinated token. The core offline SVD and MLP weight-editing procedure in Algorithm 1 remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use LURE paired data, MSCOCO captioning and POPE/OPOPE, MME, and LLaVA-Bench. The online intervention example retains the existing image-captioning task and introduces no new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and 11–13 retain their corresponding comparator sets. ITI, ActADD, and VTI are newly discussed as related work but are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix Table 6 changes the stated MME maximum new tokens from 128 to 64. v3 also adds the targeted online-intervention procedure. The PDFs do not establish whether the MME setting revision reflects a correction or rerun experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Figure 6 add a case testing whether feature projection suppresses a particular hallucinated continuation. The layer/rank ablations, difference-versus-random-vector analysis, and existing appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated three times with different random seeds and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices. No additional statistical procedure or changed run count is reported.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports an online correction from the hallucinated word 'person' to 'mountain' in Section 4.5 and Figure 6. Previously reported benchmark scores, ablation values, word frequencies, and plotted performance trends remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The projection equations, factor-decomposition assumptions, and DPO derivations are retained, including appendix Sections 6 and 8. Corrected feature labels and equation references reconcile the exposition with mathematics already stated in v1.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of HalluSpace-based hallucination mitigation, no additional inference cost for edited weights, maintained general capabilities, and a connection to DPO. Condensed contribution statements do not introduce a different central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an explanation prioritizing sentence-level CHAIRS and qualifies the CHAIRI advantage over HALC. v3 also describes an optimal low rank more accurately and softens the interpretation that HalluSpace contains LLM-prior information.

D1.justification: The documented MME generation limit is revised in Table 6, and Section 3.1 makes object substitution in hallucinated descriptions explicit. Model-specific ranks, beam settings, hardware disclosure, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 positions Nullu relative to ITI, ActADD, VTI, and the previously cited null-space editing work on detoxification. Additional citations broaden the context, while autonomous-driving and OpenVLA application references are removed.

P1.justification: v3 makes local prose revisions throughout the main text, corrects reversed feature descriptions and cross-references, and adds the feature-steering subsection, acknowledgments, and corresponding-author information. The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is redesigned to include the online-intervention panel; Figure 2 moves earlier, and Figures 3–4 receive cosmetic and labeling edits. Some floats and captions are rearranged, while the principal table structures and two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves positioning against closely related feature-steering and null-space editing methods, clarifies several explanations, and adds a focused intervention example. These are limited gains because the main empirical and theoretical evidence remains unchanged. The unexplained MME token-limit revision still leaves a reproducibility ambiguity.
